page: Amazon Web Services m8in.large is a general-purpose instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture, featuring network and EBS optimizations. It is equipped with an Intel x86_64 processor clocked at 3.9 GHz, supplying 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core through simultaneous multithreading. Memory capacity is set to 8.0 GB, providing an even 4.0 GB per vCPU distribution that aligns with typical general-purpose compute ratios.

The hardware configuration excludes local instance storage, directing all disk I/O operations to network-attached block storage. Baseline network bandwidth is provisioned at 3 Gbps, and the server operates without dedicated GPU acceleration hardware or complimentary public IPv4 addresses. By offloading virtualization and management functions to Nitro hardware, the host minimizes overhead on the dedicated vCPUs.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance targets applications that require consistent, non-burstable CPU execution with moderate memory overhead. Given the absence of local disks and accelerators, the platform is structured for distributed services, container hosting, small web application backends, and lightweight staging or development environments.
description: Amazon Web Services m8in.large is a general-purpose instance built on the AWS Nitro system architecture, featuring network and EBS optimization. The instance provides 2 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs powered by an Intel processor running at 3.9 GHz across 1 physical core with 2 threads per core. Memory capacity is configured at 8.0 GB, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include integrated local disk storage or GPU accelerators, meaning persistent storage workloads depend on network-attached storage services. Networking capabilities feature a baseline bandwidth of 3 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned. Designed for predictable throughput rather than burstable limits, m8in.large offers balanced compute and memory distribution, making it an efficient choice for moderate web serving, containerized services, microservices backends, and lightweight enterprise development tasks.
